text:
Dmitri K.: Quick Q on API behavior for generation edge cases: stop sequences vs max_tokens vs temperature/top_p + logprobs. Example request below — what should clients expect in response shape and finish_reason when stop triggers or max_tokens hit? Also logprobs if the generation gets truncated?

Dmitri K.: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-1.3",
  "prompt": "Explain Conway's Game of Life in 2 sentences.",
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "stop": ["

", "END"],
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```

Alice M.: Short answer: stop wins if it matches before hitting max_tokens. We trim stop tokens from returned text and set finish_reason = "stop".

Ben C.: Clarify: are stop matches decided on decoded text or token-level? And what about overlapping stops like "\n\n" and "\n"?

Alice M.: We match on decoded text. Implementation detail: we scan the decoded output for the earliest occurrence of any stop string as characters arrive. For overlapping stops, earliest index wins (first-occurrence).

Carla R.: Streaming edge: clients may get a chunk that ends in the middle of a stop sequence. We should guarantee we never emit the stop token in any chunk. Implementation: buffer up to len(longest_stop)-1 trailing chars; only flush when safe.

Ben C.: Another tie: if the final token completes a stop exactly at the same time as hitting max_tokens, which finish_reason do we return — "stop" or "length"?

Alice M.: Rule: if stop is detected immediately after decoding the latest token, return finish_reason = "stop". If no stop matched and we've hit the token cap, return "length". So stop takes precedence when both conditions happen simultaneously.

Dmitri K.: What about logprobs: when client requests logprobs=5, do we return logprobs for tokens that we withhold because they are part of a stop or because they're beyond max_tokens?

Carla R.: We should NOT return logprobs for tokens we don't include in the emitted token array. So logprobs map aligns 1:1 with the tokens returned in the response.

eva-bot: Spec PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/specs/pull/198 — draft includes:
- stop matching on decoded text (earliest-occurrence)
- stop tokens are excluded from emitted text
- finish_reason values: "stop", "length", "error"
- streaming: buffer longest stop len to avoid partial emission
- logprobs only for emitted tokens

Ben C.: Should we add an explicit "truncated" field to the response to indicate whether truncation happened due to "length" vs "stop"? Right now clients look at finish_reason but it's overloaded.

Carla R.: I prefer not to add new top-level fields unless necessary. finish_reason already communicates why generation stopped. We can add a short "notes" string in streaming events if we want richer info during the stream, but keep the main JSON compact.

Ben C.: Temperature/top_p interplay: doc should explicitly say both are applied. Important special-case: if temperature == 0 -> deterministically pick argmax and ignore sampling (top_p effectively ignored).

Alice M.: +1. Add wording: apply temperature scaling to logits first, then apply nucleus (top_p) sampling on the normalized probabilities. Provide example: temperature 0 => deterministic argmax; temperature >0 + top_p <1 => nucleus sampling over scaled probs.

Dmitri K.: Also need a concrete response example for clients to test against. Proposed minimal response snippet:```json
{
  "id": "g-xyz",
  "object": "generation",
  "tokens": ["In", "the", "Game", "of"],
  "text": "In the Game of",
  "logprobs": [[-1.2, -2.0, -3.1, -0.4]],
  "finish_reason": "stop"
}
```
(note: logprobs array corresponds to emitted tokens only).

Carla R.: I'll draft the PR updating the API contract and add unit tests for: overlapping stops, stop-at-cap tie, stream-chunking, and logprob alignment.

Ben C.: I can review, will also add an integration test that compares deterministic outputs for temperature=0 vs sampling.

Dmitri K.: Thanks — please @mention here when PR is up. Need this in spec before the next release cut. :thumbsup:
